rounds.text: Sportking India Ltd is trading at an attractive valuation of 10.9x P/E [E1], sitting well below the sector benchmark of 15.09x [E6], while delivering superior capital efficiency with an ROE of 18.01% and ROCE of 19.2% that comfortably outpace sector medians [E9, E10]. Operational performance is underpinned by near full capacity utilization at 99% in existing facilities [E80] and strong profitability acceleration, evidenced by a 98% TTM profit growth [E21] and a 10 percentage point expansion in quarterly operating margins to 20% [E30]. Cash generation is robust and fully validates these earnings, with operating cash flow reaching Rs 292 Cr and a high cash conversion ratio of 2.43x for Mar 2026 [E33, E34]. Furthermore, institutional participation is expanding with positive money flow and a foreign holding increase [E40, E42], while a reverse DCF indicates that the current market price incorrectly prices in negative earnings growth [E45]. Growth visibility is exceptionally strong as the 150,000 spindle Greenfield expansion in Odisha prepares for commercial production within 30 to 40 days [E76], backed by management projections that revenue will exceed INR 4,000 crores next year [E70] alongside higher structural margins from the new unit [E69]. Conceded: compounded profit growth over the last 3 years contracted by 8% [E20], and the company maintains a low 3-year average return on equity of 11.2% [E57].

Conceded: [E30]. Despite recent margin improvements, Sportking India Ltd suffers from severe medium-term operational and profit stagnation, evidenced by a 3-year compounded sales growth of just 4% [E16] and an actively negative 3-year compounded profit growth of -8% [E20]. The company's historical returns also underperform relative to expectations, as flagged by a low return on equity of just 11.2% over the last 3 years [E57]. Furthermore, shareholder returns are heavily suppressed by a meager dividend payout averaging only 7.68% of profits over the same 3-year period [E58]. The business also carries a significant historical downside risk, with a worst peak-to-trough price drawdown on record reaching -54.4% [E51]. Finally, capital-intensive expansion introduces substantial leverage and execution risks, as reflected by a massive 686.7% surge in capital work-in-progress to Rs 118 Cr [E38] alongside borrowings scaling up to Rs 545 Cr [E37].

Conceded: [E16], [E20], [E51], [E57], [E58]. While those past 3-year growth and dividend figures lagged, they ignore the explosive operational turnaround currently underway, demonstrated by a 98% surge in trailing twelve-month profit growth [E21] and a massive net profit increase of 243% year-over-year [E62]. The bear's anxiety over rising capital work-in-progress and borrowings misses the strategic reality that existing core facilities are already operating at a near-full 99% capacity [E80], making the 150,000 spindle Odisha expansion an essential and timely growth driver [E74]. Far from being a burden, this expansion brings a lucrative 30% capital subsidy returning roughly INR 200 to INR 220 crores over 5 years [E83], while management projects top-line revenue to scale past INR 4,000 crores next year [E70] alongside structurally higher unit margins [E69]. Institutional confidence is already responding positively to these catalysts, as reflected by positive money flow and growing foreign institutional holdings [E42].

Conceded: [E21], [E62]. The bull highlights surging recent profit growth and a massive year-over-year net profit increase, but this is viewed through a lens that ignores multi-year cyclical vulnerability, evidenced by an -8% compounded profit growth over the past 3 years [E20] and a low 3-year return on equity of 11.2% [E57]. The claim that existing facilities running at 99% capacity [E80] justify the massive 150,000 spindle Odisha expansion [E74] overlooks the financial strain of soaring capital work-in-progress, which climbed +686.7% to ₹118 Cr [E38], and long-term debt projected to swell to around ₹700 to ₹750 Cr by March 2027 [E84]. Furthermore, while the bull leans heavily on future revenue projections exceeding ₹4,000 crores [E70] and lucrative capital subsidies [E83], these are unverified management targets that bypass historical performance where compounded sales growth over 3 years slowed to just 4% [E16] and 5-year profit growth limped at 4% [E19]. Finally, the reliance on institutional money flow and foreign holdings [E42] as a seal of approval disregards the reality of historical volatility, marked by a severe peak-to-trough drawdown of -54.4% [E51] and an annualized volatility of 45.4% [E52].

Conceded: [E20], [E57]. The bear’s focus on historical 3-year profit growth ignores the company’s current operational transformation, as evidenced by the 98% profit growth in the trailing twelve months [E21] and a significant 10 percentage point increase in quarterly operating margins [E30]. While the bear cites rising debt [E84], it fails to acknowledge that this capital expenditure is funding a massive 150,000 spindle expansion [E74] that is already nearing commercial production [E76] and is backed by a 30% capital subsidy [E83]. The concern regarding historical sales growth [E16] is countered by the fact that existing facilities are operating at 99% capacity [E80], creating a clear bottleneck that the new Odisha project is specifically designed to resolve [E70]. Furthermore, the bear’s characterization of management targets as unverified ignores the company’s proven ability to maintain a 70 to 90-day order book [E82] and the current positive institutional money flow [E42]. Finally, while volatility [E52] is a historical reality, the company’s strong cash conversion of 2.43x [E33] and robust return on capital employed of 19.2% [E10] demonstrate a fundamental financial strength that outweighs past drawdowns.

Conceded: [E21], [E30], [E42]. While the bull points to recent trailing-twelve-month profit growth and margin expansion, it glosses over the severe historical erosion where 3-year profit growth stands at -8% [E20] and 3-year return on equity flags as low at 11.2% [E57]. The bull's reliance on near-full existing capacity [E80] to justify the massive Odisha capital expenditure ignores the sharp escalation in long-term debt expected to reach up to INR 750 crores by March 2027 [E84]. Furthermore, citing positive institutional money flow [E42] as a seal of validation overlooks the fragile ownership structure where foreign institutional holding remains a negligible 0.88% [E40] and domestic institutional holding is entirely absent at 0.00% [E41]. Finally, the high operating volatility of 45.4% [E52] coupled with a severe historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -54.4% [E51] demonstrates that the underlying cyclicality [E56] and turbulence in global cotton prices [E85] carry execution and market risks that a single quarter of margin expansion fails to erase.
